candidate.answerReason: Canceling the nonzero factor \((7x)^7\) gives \((7x)^7=2^7\), whose unique real solution is \(x=2/7\).

methods.label: Cancel a nonzero seventh power
methods.explanation:
Since \(14x=2(7x)\), the right side contains a seventh power of \(7x\). Use the power-of-a-product rule to write
\[
(7x)^{14}=2^7(7x)^7.
\]
The condition \(x\ne0\) ensures that \((7x)^7\ne0\), so dividing both sides by it is valid. This gives
\[
(7x)^7=2^7.
\]
The positive right side forces \(7x>0\). Among positive numbers, seventh powers increase with the base, so the bases must be equal: \(7x=2\). Hence \(x=2/7\).

For this value, the original equation becomes \(2^{14}=4^7\), which holds because \(4^7=(2^2)^7=2^{14}\). Thus the unique nonzero real solution is \(\boxed{\frac27}\), choice B.
